turns.content: A positive integer is Norwegian if three distinct positive divisors have sum 2022. Find and verify a concrete Norwegian number that can serve as a candidate for the minimum.
Use AM-GM on the three witnessing divisors as the sole exact minimality method, treating their product as equal to N.
Use the assumption that N is smaller than the candidate from the first step to obtain a numerical lower bound for 1/a+1/b+1/c. What does that bound imply about a?
Continue with the reciprocal bound and determine all possible values of b once a has been fixed.
Analyze the case b=3. Determine the possible values of c and show why neither can satisfy the divisor-sum equation.
Analyze the remaining case b=2, using the reciprocal bound and the divisibility relation to rule out every N<1344.
Check that the cases a>=2 and b>=4 were genuinely excluded by the strict reciprocal bound, so that the two cases just analyzed exhaust every smaller candidate.
State the smallest Norwegian number and include both the divisor witness and the minimality conclusion.
